questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A scientist measures three quantities: mass of the Sun ≈ 1.989 × 10³⁰ kg, mass of the Earth ≈ 5.972 × 10²⁴ kg, and the average distance from Earth to Sun ≈ 1.496 × 10¹¹ m.

(i) Why are these expressed in scientific notation?
(ii) Compute the ratio mass of Sun / mass of Earth.
(iii) Express your answer in scientific notation.
(iv) State the rule used for division of exponents with the same base.
questions.answer:
(i) Scientific notation makes very large (or small) numbers compact and easier to compare and compute with.
(ii) (1.989 × 10³⁰) / (5.972 × 10²⁴) = (1.989/5.972) × 10⁶ ≈ 0.333 × 10⁶ = 3.33 × 10⁵.
(iii) Sun is about 3.33 × 10⁵ times heavier than Earth (~333 000 times).
(iv) Quotient rule: a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n).

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A biologist tracks a colony that doubles every hour. Starting with 100 bacteria at t = 0:

(i) Population at t = 5 hours (in form of exponent).
(ii) Population at t = 10 hours, as a number.
(iii) State the law of exponents used.
(iv) After how many hours will the population first exceed 10 million? (Use log₂(10⁵) ≈ 16.6)
questions.answer:
(i) Population(t) = 100 × 2^t. At t = 5: 100 × 2⁵ = 100 × 32 = 3 200.
(ii) At t = 10: 100 × 2¹⁰ = 100 × 1024 = 102 400.
(iii) Product / repeated multiplication: a^m · a^n = a^(m+n). Here we're really just evaluating 2^t.
(iv) Need 100 × 2^t > 10⁷ ⇒ 2^t > 10⁵ ⇒ t > log₂(10⁵) ≈ 16.6. So first hour where population exceeds 10⁷ is t = 17 hours.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Simplify: (2³ × 2⁴) / 2⁵ , and (5²)³ × 5⁻⁴.

(i) Simplify (2³ × 2⁴) / 2⁵.
(ii) Simplify (5²)³ × 5⁻⁴.
(iii) State the laws of exponents used in each.
(iv) Evaluate (2³)² × 4 × 2⁻⁴.
questions.answer:
(i) (2³ × 2⁴) / 2⁵ = 2^(3+4-5) = 2² = 4.
(ii) (5²)³ × 5⁻⁴ = 5^(2·3) × 5⁻⁴ = 5⁶ × 5⁻⁴ = 5² = 25.
(iii) Used: product rule a^m · a^n = a^(m+n); quotient rule a^m/a^n = a^(m−n); power-of-a-power (a^m)^n = a^(mn); negative exponent a^(−n) = 1/a^n.
(iv) (2³)² × 4 × 2⁻⁴ = 2⁶ × 2² × 2⁻⁴ = 2^(6+2−4) = 2⁴ = 16.

Read the passage and answer the questions.

A classmate writes: '√(a² + b²) = a + b' for all real a, b.

(i) Test the claim with a = 3, b = 4.
(ii) Hence is the claim true in general?
(iii) What is the CORRECT formula for √(a² + b²) when a, b are positive?
(iv) Does the claim hold for any specific case (other than trivial a = 0 or b = 0)?
questions.answer:
(i) √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5. a + b = 3 + 4 = 7. So 5 ≠ 7 ✗.
(ii) The claim is FALSE in general.
(iii) There's no simple algebraic simplification — √(a² + b²) cannot be written as a + b. For positive a, b, this is just the Pythagorean-style 'hypotenuse' expression. For specific values you compute the numerical sum, square, and take a root.
(iv) Only when one of a, b is zero: if a = 0, then √(0 + b²) = |b| = a + b (for b ≥ 0). Otherwise the strict inequality √(a² + b²) < a + b holds for positive a, b.

Read the passage and answer the questions.

A cell biologist observes that bacteria are about 10⁻⁶ m wide and viruses are about 10⁻⁸ m wide.

(i) Express the bacterium width in micrometres (1 μm = 10⁻⁶ m).
(ii) How many viruses can fit across one bacterium?
(iii) State the property of exponents used.
(iv) If a cell is 10⁻⁵ m wide, how many bacteria fit across it?
questions.answer:
(i) 10⁻⁶ m = 1 μm. So a bacterium is about 1 μm wide.
(ii) (bacterium width)/(virus width) = 10⁻⁶/10⁻⁸ = 10⁻⁶⁻(⁻⁸) = 10² = 100.
(iii) Quotient rule for exponents: a^m / a^n = a^(m − n).
(iv) 10⁻⁵/10⁻⁶ = 10¹ = 10 bacteria across one cell.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Simplify and reason: (a^m × a^n) / a^(m+n) where a > 0, m and n integers.

(i) Simplify the expression.
(ii) What rule is used?
(iii) Compute the expression for a = 3, m = 5, n = 2.
(iv) What is a⁰ (where a ≠ 0)? Why?
questions.answer:
(i) (a^m × a^n)/a^(m+n) = a^(m+n)/a^(m+n) = a⁰ = 1.
(ii) Product rule (a^m · a^n = a^(m+n)) combined with quotient rule (a^p / a^p = 1).
(iii) a = 3, m = 5, n = 2: (3⁵ × 3²)/3⁷ = (243 × 9)/2187 = 2187/2187 = 1 ✓.
(iv) a⁰ = 1 for a ≠ 0, by extending the quotient rule: a^m/a^m = a^(m−m) = a⁰, and also a^m/a^m = 1, so a⁰ = 1. (0⁰ is undefined.)
